lead:
President Tinubu ordered an investigation into the deaths of 37 detainees held after illegal mining raids in Niger State, where the state cancelled an APC rally and suspended the Civil Defence commandant.

The day in brief: Information Minister Mohammed Idris promised a thorough, transparent and impartial inquiry and said no one found culpable would be shielded. The APC campaign told Atiku Abubakar to quit the race after the Mambilla arbitration award flagged a $500,000 payment to his former wife, and the Court of Appeal, by a split decision, reversed the ruling that had stalled the registration of Peter Obi's NDC. Central Bank data showed the current account surplus rising 68 per cent to $7.54 billion on stronger exports and diaspora remittances, and the stock market closed above N162 trillion for the first time. The government and the CBN signed a pact to coordinate fiscal and monetary policy, INEC began recruiting 1.4 million temporary election workers, and the foreign minister warned diplomats against lecturing Nigeria on democracy. In Paris, President Macron hosted Tinubu to a private dinner.

items.h: Tinubu orders probe of mining suspects' deaths; Niger cancels APC rally
items.s: Information Minister Mohammed Idris promised a thorough, transparent and impartial investigation into the deaths of people arrested in enforcement operations against illegal mining in the Wushishi area of Niger State, and said anyone found culpable would not be shielded. Niger State cancelled Saturday's APC rally in Minna and suspended the NSCDC commandant after 37 detainees died.

items.h: Mambilla award flags $500,000 payment to Atiku's ex-wife; APC tells him to quit
items.s: The ICC tribunal's award in the Mambilla arbitration said a $500,000 transfer in 2003 by a witness's company to Atiku Abubakar's then wife raised significant red flags. The APC presidential campaign council seized on the finding and called on Atiku, the ADC candidate, to withdraw from the 2027 race, saying the proceedings raised serious questions about his role in the project.

items.h: Appeal Court reverses deregistration of Obi's NDC
items.s: In a 2-1 decision, the Court of Appeal in Abuja set aside a ruling of the Federal High Court in Lokoja that had suspended its own earlier order for INEC to register the Nigeria Democratic Congress, pending a fresh hearing of a dispute over the party's logo. The judgment clears the way for the party on whose platform Peter Obi is running.

items.h: Current account surplus rises 68% to $7.54bn
items.s: Nigeria's surplus on the current account jumped by about two-thirds in the April-June quarter, to $7.54 billion from $4.49 billion, and stood almost 46 per cent above the same quarter of 2025, according to provisional central bank figures. Higher earnings from oil, gas and refined fuel exports helped, as did money sent home by Nigerians abroad, which climbed nearly 10 per cent to $5.82 billion.

items.h: NGX market value passes N162trn for first time
items.s: The Nigerian Exchange closed the week at a record market capitalisation of N162.16 trillion, up N2.27 trillion in a day, as the All-Share Index rose 1.42 per cent to an all-time high of 249,804.56 points. The previous record of N161.8 trillion was set on 13 May.

items.h: Macron hosts Tinubu at private dinner in Paris
items.s: French President Emmanuel Macron hosted President Tinubu to a private dinner at the Élysée Palace on Thursday night, presidential spokesman Bayo Onanuga said on X. He said the dinner reflected the enduring relationship between the two countries, and both leaders pledged to deepen bilateral cooperation.

items.h: FG and CBN sign pact on fiscal and monetary coordination
items.s: The Ministry of Finance and the CBN signed a memorandum in Abuja that sets up regular consultations, data sharing and joint forecasts between fiscal and monetary authorities. Finance Minister Taiwo Oyedele said the aim is to bring inflation down sustainably and give investors greater policy consistency as the CBN prepares for inflation targeting.

items.h: INEC begins recruiting 1.4 million ad hoc staff
items.s: INEC opened its online portal to recruit about 1.4 million ad hoc staff to work in more than 176,000 polling units at the 2027 elections. The presidential and National Assembly elections are scheduled for 16 January 2027, with governorship and state assembly polls to follow.

items.h: Foreign minister warns envoys against unguarded comments on elections
items.s: Meeting ambassadors in Abuja, Foreign Minister Bianca Odumegwu-Ojukwu cautioned foreign missions to keep their public comments measured in the run-up to the 2027 polls, and said Nigeria would not welcome careless or belittling statements or uninvited advice on how to run its democracy.

items.h: Bandits kill 13 in three Zamfara villages
items.s: Bandits killed at least 13 people in three villages of Dansadau Emirate in Maru, Zamfara, in reprisal after local vigilantes killed a bandit leader and his men. A resident who asked not to be named said the gunmen targeted the villages over the killing, and called for urgent action on insecurity.

items.h: Mother and children die in Okrika house fire
items.s: A mother and her children were burned to death when fire engulfed their house in Okochiri community, Okrika, Rivers State, in the early hours of Friday while the family slept. Early reports said four children died; police later put the toll at the mother and three children. Community youths put out the fire, whose cause was not confirmed.

items.h: Atiku urges Tinubu to cut fuel prices and offers his ideas
items.s: At a press conference in Abuja, Atiku Abubakar said palliatives cannot replace sound policies that bring down the cost of living, and urged the President to cut petrol prices, which he said have pushed up transport, food and production costs since subsidy removal. He offered to share his proposals, saying Tinubu could rename them and take the credit.

items.h: Emir Sanusi urges Kano residents to buy Dangote refinery shares
items.s: The Emir of Kano, Muhammadu Sanusi II, urged individuals and businesses in Kano to invest in the Dangote refinery IPO, calling share ownership a path to long-term wealth. Defending the project against critics, he challenged them to raise the estimated $22 billion it would take to build a competing refinery.

items.h: Dangote refinery sourced 60% of its crude locally
items.s: The Dangote refinery's IPO prospectus shows it bought about 60 per cent of its crude from Nigeria in the 12 months to June 2026, relying heavily on the naira-for-crude scheme to cut its foreign exchange exposure. It processed roughly 26.4 million tonnes of crude in the period.

items.h: Tinubu orders 180-day roadmap for Digital Free Zones
items.s: President Tinubu directed that a roadmap for the full launch of Nigeria's Digital Free Zones be ready within 180 days. The scheme aims to let Nigerian technology and service companies raise global capital, employ Nigerians and sell to international markets without moving their businesses and intellectual property abroad.

items.h: $12m enterprise centre unveiled in Abuja
items.s: SMEDAN, the UNDP and South Korea, through KOICA, broke ground on the $12 million Abuja Centre for Entrepreneurship at SMEDAN's headquarters. The hub is meant to help young people, women, start-ups and small businesses turn ideas into viable enterprises and create jobs.

items.h: 50MW power project to supply Idu industrial area
items.s: Ground was broken on a 50-megawatt power project for the Idu industrial zone in Abuja, developed by Welbeck Electricity Distribution, the Abuja Electricity Distribution Company and Shell Gas. It will be built in phases, beginning with 10MW, to give industries and businesses steady supply.

items.h: KASU lecturers suspend strike
items.s: ASUU's Kaduna State University chapter suspended its strike after the state government approved implementation of the 2025 federal government-ASUU agreement, following a congress on 17 September. Lecturers at the University of Benin also suspended an indefinite strike after management promised to pay outstanding allowances.

items.h: Gombe restricts movement for Saturday by-election
items.s: Gombe police restricted movement and closed commercial activities in Gombe, Kwami and Funakaye from 6am to 6pm on Saturday for the federal constituency by-election. Kano police announced a similar restriction in Dawakin Kudu for the state assembly by-election there.

items.h: ICPC questions Ekiti APC House candidate over alleged fraud
items.s: Toyin Okoro, the APC's candidate for Ise-Orun/Ikere/Ekiti South-West federal constituency and a former senior legislative aide to Speaker Tajudeen Abbas, appeared before the ICPC in Abuja, where he was questioned over alleged fraud and abuse of office.

items.h: Fitch says CBN holding company rules could force bank restructuring
items.s: The CBN's draft framework for bank holding companies may oblige some Nigerian lenders to rework who owns what, move subsidiaries abroad under new parents and reorganise operations, Fitch Ratings said in a mid-September report on the cross-border growth of African banking groups.

items.h: Mafab plans to sell 5G assets to MTN
items.s: Mafab Communications, backed by businessman Musbahu Muhammad Bashir, plans to sell its 5G spectrum, bought for $273.6 million and covering blocks in the 2.1GHz and 3.5GHz bands, to MTN Nigeria, subject to regulatory approval. Mafab was one of the country's pioneer 5G licensees in 2022.

items.h: Jonathan calls for unified federal and state civil service pay
items.s: Former President Goodluck Jonathan called for the harmonisation of structures and salaries in the federal and state civil services, saying workers doing similar jobs should not be paid differently. He spoke in Yenagoa at the foundation-laying for the Bayelsa association of retired permanent secretaries' secretariat.

items.h: Police repatriate Chinese fugitive wanted over rosewood smuggling
items.s: The police, through Interpol's National Central Bureau in Abuja, sent Chinese fugitive Zhang Shijie back to Guangzhou. He was wanted by Chinese customs over the alleged smuggling of about 1,400 tonnes of endangered African rosewood.

items.h: EFCC probes man caught with fake $212,200 in Kano
items.s: The EFCC's Kano office began investigating Usaini Ibrahim, arrested by the NDLEA on Maiduguri Road, Kano, on 3 September with counterfeit US dollars with a face value of $212,200. The NDLEA handed him and the fake notes to the commission.

items.h: FG moves to clear Bida-Kutigi gridlock and Lagos truck parking
items.s: On President Tinubu's directive, the government ordered urgent measures to clear a long traffic gridlock on the Bida–Kutigi corridor in Niger State and to remove illegally parked trucks from port access roads in Lagos. His transport aide, Adetokunbo Ade-John, joined officials on the road.

items.h: Plateau cracks down on houses without toilets
items.s: The Plateau Environmental Protection and Sanitation Agency began a crackdown on houses in Jos South without functional toilets, giving households seven days to build them or face prosecution, after months of community engagement and public education.

items.h: Hajj operators demand probe of private slot allocation
items.s: Private Hajj operators asked President Tinubu to order an independent review of how 15,000 private-sector seats for the 2027 pilgrimage were allocated, alleging that 5,000 of them were diverted to two new companies linked to Kano and Adamawa.

items.h: Group urges Wike and APC to protect party unity
items.s: State coordinators of the Renewed Hope Ambassadors urged FCT Minister Nyesom Wike to support APC structures and avoid actions that could weaken the party or unsettle its governors' commitment to President Tinubu's re-election.

items.h: Edo council chairman criticised over party caps directive
items.s: Blessing Albert Ebhodaghe, chairman of Esan West local government in Edo, was criticised after a video showed him warning commercial drivers in motor parks not to wear caps of rival parties and directing them to wear APC caps.

items.h: Christian youths endorse APM's Haske in Adamawa
items.s: The Adamawa State Youth Christian Movement for Change endorsed Abdulrahman Bashir Haske, the APM's candidate, for the 2027 governorship election. Haske came third in the APC primary in May before moving to the APM and winning its ticket.

items.h: KADGIS says it has resolved 5,000 land disputes
items.s: The Kaduna Geographic Information Service said it has resolved more than 5,000 land disputes and restored over 150 titles that were unjustly revoked in the past three and a half years, director-general Bashir Garba Ibrahim told a town hall.

items.h: Finchglow plans flying school at Gateway Airport
items.s: Finchglow Holdings plans a private flying school at Gateway International Agro-Cargo Airport in Ogun State, subject to regulatory approval, to meet growing demand for pilots in Nigeria and West Africa, group managing director Bankole Bernard said.

items.h: World Bank mobilises record $112bn in private capital
items.s: In the 2026 fiscal year the World Bank Group attracted a record $112 billion of private money into developing countries alongside its own lending, more than three times the $35 billion of 2022. African projects drew $22 billion, almost two and a half times the figure four years ago, and the bank's guarantees reached a record $25 billion.

items.h: Mbappe leaves Nike for On
items.s: Kylian Mbappé ended his long partnership with Nike and signed with Swiss sportswear brand On, which is entering football. The France captain will be the centrepiece of the venture and work with its teams on future boots and apparel.
